freeze_rule: No proposed event is freeze-ready until all required fields are completed and independently reviewed. If frozen on 2026-10-17, the candidate five-year observation end would be 2031-10-17; this is not an active forecast horizon while freeze_at is null.

shared_adjudication_rules.review_requirement: Two independent reviewers for any ground-truth outcome; source/version/date and exact endpoint match must be checked separately. A third reviewer adjudicates disagreement.
shared_adjudication_rules.historical_snapshot_rule: The 2026-10-16 radar wording remains qualitative editorial evidence only. These event proposals were created after that cutoff and cannot be backdated into that snapshot.

items.source_title: Joint KV-cache scheduling and speculative decoding under heterogeneous, changing load
items.proposed_event: A versioned joint cache/scheduling/speculation policy is independently reproduced on a held-out, time-varying workload and improves a preselected end-to-end goodput or tail-latency endpoint over separately tuned component policies while meeting the same memory and output-quality constraints.
success_evidence: Public versioned implementation and workload trace
Predeclared quality and SLO noninferiority margins
Independent reproduction with raw per-workload measurements
against_or_refutation: Matched evaluation shows no qualifying gain
Gain disappears under held-out load or equal-memory accounting
Quality or tail-SLO constraint is violated
Independent reproduction fails
missing_definition_fields: Primary metric and numerical noninferiority/superiority margins
Holdout split and unit of analysis
Treatment of failures and repeated runs
reviewer_decisions_required: Does the held-out trace represent the claimed load regime?
Do quality and memory constraints match?

items.source_title: Repository-scale verified code generation and repair
items.proposed_event: On a preregistered set of held-out repositories, an approach produces more independently accepted issue-resolving patches that satisfy hidden regressions and an audited formal specification than a matched baseline, without increasing correctness-critical failures under a fixed compute budget.
success_evidence: Frozen repository/task set and versioned patches
Hidden test results and proof-checker outputs where applicable
Matched baseline, budget, and repository-level uncertainty
against_or_refutation: No improvement on held-out repositories
Formal proof passes but intended behavior or hidden tests fail
Gain vanishes under equal budget
Specification audit finds material omissions
missing_definition_fields: Task inclusion and repository holdout rules
How proof-bearing and test-only tasks are stratified
reviewer_decisions_required: Does the specification capture issue intent?
Are proof and test outcomes comparable?
Are patches independently judged without model self-evaluation?

items.source_title: Artifact-level process verification for multi-agent execution
items.proposed_event: A prespecified process-verification signal or intervention improves independently adjudicated artifact correctness over no-verifier and deterministic-check baselines on held-out task families at matched runtime/context cost, with false-accept and false-reject rates reported.
against_or_refutation: No improvement after cost matching
Verifier accepts invalid artifacts above the prespecified bound
Benefit is confined to seen task families
Independent adjudicators disagree beyond the frozen tolerance
reviewer_decisions_required: Were verifier signals frozen before outcome review?

items.source_title: Tight, certified filters for fully adaptive differential privacy
items.proposed_event: A new filter is proved sound for an explicitly enumerated adaptive mechanism family and parameter regime, strictly improves a frozen privacy-utility or bound-tightness criterion over the strongest applicable certified baseline, and has an independently checked numerical implementation certificate.
success_evidence: Explicit covered and excluded parameter ranges
against_or_refutation: Counterexample violates soundness
No strict improvement over the matched baseline
Certificate is invalid or omits numerical error
Claim relies on adaptivity outside the theorem assumptions
missing_definition_fields: Exact mechanism family and parameter region
Definition of tightness/utility and strict margin
reviewer_decisions_required: Do all adaptive choices satisfy the theorem hypotheses?
Is comparison against the strongest applicable bound?
Does theorem scope match the claimed deployment?

items.source_title: Scientific agents that move from ideas to independently verified evidence
items.proposed_event: On a prospectively frozen set of research questions, an agent completes a falsifiable action whose raw artifact is independently reproduced and whose result changes a preregistered scientific decision, at a declared resource cost; proposal quality alone does not count.
success_evidence: Frozen question, hypotheses, action, and stopping rule
Blinded decision rubric and recorded action cost
against_or_refutation: Only question/proposal ratings improve
Action is not executable or does not discriminate hypotheses
Independent reproduction fails
Evidence does not alter the prespecified uncertainty or decision criterion
reviewer_decisions_required: Is the question genuinely frozen before outcomes?
Is evidence independent of the agent's own claims?
Is novelty reviewed against prior art?

items.source_title: Conflict-aware persistent memory for multi-agent systems
items.proposed_event: Under a fixed memory/context budget and versioned stream of contradictory evidence, a conflict-aware memory system improves downstream factual or task correctness over non-conflict-aware memory baselines on held-out tasks while reducing neither important contradiction visibility nor provenance fidelity.
success_evidence: Frozen evidence-update tasks with ground-truth conflict relations
Independent task scoring and held-out replication
against_or_refutation: No downstream gain at equal memory budget
System hides or merges material contradictions
Provenance or update order changes the answer incorrectly
Gain fails on held-out evidence sequences
reviewer_decisions_required: Are all baselines under equal context limits?
Does the test distinguish recall from correctness?

items.source_title: KV-cache eviction and retention with explicit quality guarantees
items.proposed_event: A retention/eviction method uses less KV memory than a frozen baseline while satisfying a prespecified output-quality noninferiority margin across held-out model/task/workload strata, with tail latency and recomputation cost reported.
success_evidence: Independent task-level replication and resource measurements
against_or_refutation: Quality falls beyond the margin
Memory savings disappear after metadata/recompute costs
Results fail on held-out tasks or model families
Baseline was not comparably tuned
reviewer_decisions_required: Are eviction baselines current and matched?
Are samples independent at the task/model level?

items.source_title: Runtime KV placement across heterogeneous memory tiers
items.proposed_event: A runtime placement policy improves a predeclared throughput or tail-latency objective over a fixed-tier policy under equal capacity and workload while including transfer, contention, preemption, and quality costs.
success_evidence: Independent reproduction with SLO and quality reports
against_or_refutation: Transfer or contention eliminates gains
Tail SLO or output quality degrades beyond margin
Improvement requires extra memory/capacity
Independent deployment replay fails
reviewer_decisions_required: Are all tier capacities held fixed?

items.source_title: Formal verification across realistic repository dependency closures
items.proposed_event: A verification method increases independently audited, semantically valid proof coverage for changes whose full repository dependency closure is included, without relying on incomplete specifications, on held-out projects against a matched verifier baseline.
success_evidence: Pinned project revisions and dependency closures
Held-out project replication and cost record
against_or_refutation: Proofs fail when dependencies are restored
Specification omits changed behavior
No gain over matched baseline
Coverage gain relies on exclusions or manual proof repair
reviewer_decisions_required: Does proof entail the intended behavior?

items.source_title: Long-horizon software engineering agents on held-out repositories
items.proposed_event: On a frozen held-out repository task set, an agent completes more independently accepted, regression-safe issue resolutions than a matched baseline under fixed wall-clock/compute limits, with task duration and failure severity reported.
success_evidence: Hidden regression suite and human acceptance criteria
against_or_refutation: Success is limited to benchmark-visible tests
Regression or issue-intent mismatch offsets gains
No gain at equal budget
Results fail on held-out repositories
missing_definition_fields: Handling of partial patches and regressions
reviewer_decisions_required: Are long tasks and repeated issue families clustered?

items.source_title: AI/software supply-chain risk measured against confirmed incidents
items.proposed_event: An independently audited study links a prespecified AI/software supply-chain control to a lower rate of externally confirmed, scope-matched compromise incidents than a defined comparator, with exposure denominators, ascertainment, and confounding handled explicitly.
success_evidence: Public incident criteria and independent confirmation records
Independent incident coding and sensitivity analysis
against_or_refutation: No association under the prespecified design
Effect disappears under ascertainment sensitivity
Incidents cannot be attributed to the control
Only threat taxonomies or discussion volume are available
reviewer_decisions_required: Could reporting or adoption selection explain the effect?

items.source_title: Instance-adaptive incremental view maintenance beyond fixed query-optimal thresholds
items.proposed_event: Only a new theorem or independently reproducible implementation showing a strict, amortized objective improvement over the published heavy/light rebalancing and major-rebalance baseline in a precisely stated workload regime would count as progress; changing skew alone does not qualify.
success_evidence: Explicit query/data/update model and workload regime
Comparison to the source's rebalancing guarantees
against_or_refutation: Existing theorem already implies the claimed benefit
Any gain disappears after rebuild/migration costs
No strict objective improvement over fixed-query baseline
Claim depends only on skew adaptation already handled by prior work
reviewer_decisions_required: Is the contribution outside Abo-Khamis et al.'s amortized rebalancing?
Is claimed objective asymptotically or practically stronger?
Does the evidence avoid hindsight selection?
